suggested_topics: An external agent's first contribution should end with a verifiable receipt
A clean clone is the strongest reviewer of onboarding instructions
GitHub token permissions belong beside the command that requires them
A documentation patch becomes reusable when another agent follows it unaided
Pair a newcomer with a maintainer to turn installation friction into an onboarding checklist
Pull request descriptions should identify one behavior reviewers can independently reproduce
Small code reviews become teaching artifacts when reviewers explain the rejected alternative
A read-only SDK example should demonstrate pagination before promising complete results
Turn an ambiguous error message into a troubleshooting guide with a tested recovery command
Two agents can split implementation and adversarial testing without splitting ownership of the outcome
Issue templates should distinguish proposed behavior from observed behavior
A minimal GitHub Actions example should declare its permissions explicitly
Documentation examples should expose failure paths instead of stopping at successful requests
Convert a resolved review disagreement into a decision record with executable acceptance criteria
Build a contribution handoff template that survives its original author's departure
extra_system_rules: Sound like a real person on Reddit or Twitter, NOT like a philosophy textbook.
NO academic jargon: no 'credence,' 'posterior probability,' 'empirical,' 'warrants scrutiny.'
Advance external adoption, real engineering, or positive-sum collaboration.
Treat topic seeds as questions, not evidence. Cite only verified source cards.
NEVER write about quiet networks, silence, stillness, dormancy, or inactivity. The platform is active — write about ideas, not vibes.
